description:
The adopter-facing command reference is the single home for the archive and document command behaviour this epic changes, so the reference reads as one coherent document instead of a pile of independent edits.

## Background

Each behaviour change in this epic that an adopter observes from the command line lands in the same reference document: archive destination naming, out-of-root artifact classification, directory-typed link targets, the in-content citation warning and the declared universe it scans, the subcommand that resolves an issue's canonical artifact directory, and the advisory conformance report. Dividing that document among the tasks that produce those behaviours would leave its structure to whichever task edited it last, while an adopter-facing fact has one canonical home.

This issue therefore owns the command reference outright, and the tasks that change the underlying behaviour write only their code and test files. Each of those behaviours is implemented and covered by the time this work starts, so the reference is written against shipped behaviour rather than against intent.

The command behaviour belongs here; the directory convention and the development-area classification do not. Those have their own canonical adopter home, and this reference cites it rather than restating it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The command reference states that an archive destination directory is named from a membership label or a bare short id, with no title-derived name.
- [hard] REQ-02: The command reference states that a selected root outside the configured development root is retained: no destination is scheduled for it, its source is left in place, and no unmanaged-selected-root blocker is reported for it.
- [hard] REQ-03: The command reference describes a link target resolving to a directory as navigation rather than as a blocked artifact.
- [hard] REQ-04: The command reference lists the in-content citation warning code and describes the declared scan universe the warning is raised from.
- [hard] REQ-05: The command reference documents the subcommand that prints an issue's canonical artifact directory, including its area argument.
- [hard] REQ-06: The command reference documents the conformance report, including that it mutates nothing and blocks no state transition.
- [hard] REQ-07: The directory convention and the development-area classification are cited from the canonical adopter reference rather than restated in the command reference.

## Notes

REQ-02 described archival by copy until escalation E9 replaced that mechanism with retention, for the reasons recorded in `@/issue/8e071e18/decision/D-14`. Documenting copy behaviour would teach an adopter something the command no longer does. Owner-approved amendment.
title: Document the epic's command-surface changes in the adopter command reference
